claims.title: Engineer sign-in credentials may be readable on the corporate network
claims.description: `flow:entity:duty-engineer>process:dispatch-console>open-console` carries the duty engineer's sign-in to `process:dispatch-console`, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If that attribute resolves to no effective transport protection, an attacker with observation capability on `boundary:corporate-network` can intercept credentials between the engineer browser and console. Those credentials could then be used in a separate identity attack to reach the console and its downstream dispatch API interactions; this draft does not assert that the flow is plaintext.

quotes.text: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:duty-engineer>process:dispatch-console>open-console` has unverified transport protection, although the attacker needs a position on the corporate-network path. Impact is high because the flow carries credentials, which can unlock the dispatch console and its calls toward `process:dispatch-api`.

mitigations.summary: Require HTTPS for the console sign-in flow
mitigations.detail: Establish and enforce TLS 1.2+ for `flow:entity:duty-engineer>process:dispatch-console>open-console`, redirect insecure requests, and record the verified transport configuration.

mitigations.summary: Limit the value of intercepted credentials
mitigations.detail: Use phishing-resistant MFA and short-lived session credentials so a captured sign-in secret alone is insufficient for durable access.

claims.title: Dispatch requests may be exposed across the corporate-to-control-plane boundary
claims.description: `flow:process:dispatch-console>process:dispatch-api>dispatch-requests` crosses from the corporate network to the production control plane, carries dispatch actions, and has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If transport confidentiality is absent, an attacker able to observe that boundary-crossing path can intercept requests concerning crew movements and depot work. The disclosed operational information can guide later targeting of the live estate reached through `process:dispatch-api`; this is conditional on the unresolved transport attribute, not an assertion that the flow is cleartext.

quotes.text: The console and the API are served from different origins, so the API answers the console cross-origin.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional: the flow crosses a trust boundary and its encryption in transit is unstated, but interception requires access to that corporate-to-control-plane path. Impact is medium because the flow exposes business-critical dispatch actions affecting crews and depot work.

mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:dispatch-console>process:dispatch-api>dispatch-requests` to verified TLS and ensure the browser validates the API identity.

mitigations.summary: Minimize operational detail in request payloads
mitigations.detail: Use narrowly scoped operation identifiers where the API can resolve details server-side, reducing sensitive dispatch information exposed on the path.

claims.title: Live job status may be readable over an unverified WebSocket
claims.description: `flow:process:dispatch-console>process:dispatch-api>live-job-status` crosses from `boundary:corporate-network` to `boundary:production-control-plane` and carries live job status, yet both its WebSocket authentication and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the socket is not protected with TLS, an on-path observer can intercept the live crew status displayed to engineers. The accumulated operational status can reveal current field activity and support targeting of the dispatch operations exposed through `process:dispatch-api`; the threat is conditional on the unresolved TLS state.

quotes.text: Nobody wrote down whether that socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after it is open.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because this is a boundary-crossing WebSocket with unverified TLS, though an attacker still needs access to the path. Impact is medium because live job status is business-critical operational data and exposes crew activity in real time.

mitigations.detail: Use WSS backed by TLS 1.2+ for `flow:process:dispatch-console>process:dispatch-api>live-job-status` and reject plaintext WebSocket upgrades.

mitigations.summary: Bind and revalidate the engineer session
mitigations.detail: Authenticate the WebSocket handshake and enforce session expiry and authorization checks for subscriptions so only the entitled engineer receives status data.

claims.title: Archived partner schedules may be exposed while written to the file store
claims.description: `flow:process:schedule-importer>store:schedule-archive>store-schedule-documents` writes every downloaded partner XML schedule document to `store:schedule-archive`, but its transport protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the write path is unencrypted, an attacker able to observe the corporate-network storage path can intercept tomorrow's planned work. That disclosure provides advance operational information that can be correlated with the importer and dispatch workflows; it is conditional on the unverified transport control.

quotes.text: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the protocol and transport protection of the corporate file-store write are unstated, although the attacker needs a corporate-network observation position. Impact is medium because every archive document contains business-critical planned work.

mitigations.detail: Use an authenticated encrypted file-sharing protocol for `flow:process:schedule-importer>store:schedule-archive>store-schedule-documents` and document the protocol and TLS configuration.

mitigations.summary: Restrict archive access to the importer
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated archive principal with least-privilege write access and separate read roles for approved schedule consumers.

claims.title: The importer's static API token may be intercepted en route to the dispatch API
claims.description: `flow:process:schedule-importer>process:dispatch-api>post-work-orders` crosses from the corporate network into the production control plane and has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. The importer presents an API token on this path, and the token is stated to be unrotated since the importer was built. If transport protection is absent, a path observer can intercept that credential together with parsed work orders; holding the token enables a separate spoofing or tampering attack against `process:dispatch-api` rather than merely disclosure.

quotes.text: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls. It presents an API token. That token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the boundary-crossing flow has unverified encryption, but interception requires access to its path. Impact is high because the intercepted static API token can provide durable access to the dispatch API that controls business-critical crew and depot work.

mitigations.summary: Protect the importer API call with mutually authenticated TLS
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ and mTLS on `flow:process:schedule-importer>process:dispatch-api>post-work-orders` so neither work orders nor the bearer credential are observable on the path.

mitigations.summary: Replace and rotate the static API token
mitigations.detail: Issue short-lived, narrowly scoped importer credentials from a managed secret store and immediately rotate the token that has never been rotated.

claims.title: Dispatch database traffic may expose crew personal data inside the control plane
claims.description: `flow:process:dispatch-api>store:dispatch-database>read-write-job-orders` carries job orders, crew names, and crew mobile numbers, while its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the database connection lacks effective transport encryption, an attacker with a position on the production-control-plane path can intercept PII and dispatch records without using the API's normal read path. The data can then identify and target crews and disclose the operational records held by `store:dispatch-database`; this is conditional on the unresolved connection protection.

quotes.text: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database. That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional: the database transport is unverified, but an attacker must first obtain an observation position inside the non-internet-facing production control plane. Impact is medium because the connection carries crew PII and business-critical job-order data.

mitigations.detail: Configure TLS with certificate validation for `flow:process:dispatch-api>store:dispatch-database>read-write-job-orders` and require an authenticated database principal.
Segment the database path and limit packet-capture and network-administration privileges to reduce the population able to observe API-to-database traffic.

claims.title: A dispatch-database storage copy may disclose crew records if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:dispatch-database` holds job orders, crew names, and crew mobile numbers, while its `encryption_at_rest` state is unknown. If that unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker obtaining a database disk, backup, snapshot, or decommissioned storage copy can read the records directly without authenticating through `process:dispatch-api`. The disclosure supports identification and targeting of field crews and exposes the dispatch corpus; this draft is conditional and does not claim the database is presently unencrypted.

quotes.text: How the database is protected at rest is not written down anywhere.
That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:dispatch-database` has unverified encryption at rest and storage copies can be accessed outside the application's normal controls. Impact is medium because the store contains crew names, mobile numbers, and business-critical job-order records, while its classification is not stated.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for the dispatch database
mitigations.detail: Establish the actual `encryption_at_rest` state, then require managed-key encryption for `store:dispatch-database`, including backups, snapshots, replicas, and decommissioned media.
Use separate least-privilege roles for database administration, backup export, and key use, and audit snapshot creation and restoration.

claims.title: Schedule archive copies may disclose planned work if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:schedule-archive` retains every XML schedule document downloaded from the scheduling partner, and its `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If the corporate file-store folder is not encrypted at rest, an attacker who obtains a backup, disk, or other storage-layer copy can read the archived schedules without using `process:schedule-importer`. Those documents reveal planned work in advance and can be correlated with the importer and dispatch API workflow; this is conditional on resolving the archive's at-rest protection.

quotes.text: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS and parses the XML document it gets back. It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:schedule-archive` has no verified at-rest protection, allowing a storage-copy attack if encryption is absent. Impact is medium because the archive retains business-critical planned work documents for the scheduling workflow.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the schedule archive and its operational copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the archive's encryption posture and require managed-key encryption for `store:schedule-archive`, backups, snapshots, and any replicated file-store copies.
Apply deny-by-default file-store permissions, granting the importer write access and only explicitly approved services or staff read access to retained schedule documents.
